newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA NOTCH UP DAVIS CUP QUARTER FINAL WIN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRALIA NOTCH UP DAVIS CUP QUARTER FINAL WIN.

text.p: World number one pair Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde gave Australia an unbeatable 3-0 lead in the Davis Cup quarter final against the Czech Republic with a four-set win in the doubles on Saturday.
But the four-time Wimbledon doubles champions were forced to come from one set down after unfancied Czech pair Martin Damm and David Rikl provided a sterner than expected test at Memorial Drive.
The Australians lost the first set before fighting back to win 4-6 6-1 7-5 6-4 on the grass centre court after the start of the match was delayed for more than one hour because of rain.
Australia earned a semi-final berth against either the United States or the Netherlands away from home between September 19-21.
Non-playing captain John Newcombe said Australia's victory proved their renaissance in Davis Cup after a disappointing run of results in recent years.
"We are back and we're looking forward to going to the U.S. and we want to take on (Pete) Sampras and whoever else they give us to play," Newcombe told reporters after the doubles match.
"It has been a tough three years for us. We lost a tie in Hungary 18 months ago and we were getting some criticism."
"We made a commitment then and I am proud of the team and the job they have done," he said.
The U.S. emerged as Australia's likely semi-final hosts after they secured a 2-0 lead over the Dutch in the first round of singles matches in Newport Beach, Calfornia on Friday.
Australia's loss in Hungary meant they were relegated from the elite world group of the Davis Cup for the first time but they won promotion at the first attempt the following year.
Australians Pat Rafter and big-serving Mark Philippoussis both won their singles rubbers against the Czechs on Friday to set the home side on the way to a comprehensive victory.
Woodbridge was Australia's weak link in the opening set of the doubles match, twice dropping his serve to allow the Czech pair an ideal start.
But the Australians gradually asserted their domination as Woodbridge found his timing and touch with both his serve and service returns.

The Czechs, already weakened by the decision of several top players including veteran Petr Korda to make themselves unavailable, suffered another setback on Friday when singles player Jiri Novak was forced to withdraw because of a virus.

In Novak's absence, the Czech's played Damm and Davis Cup debutant Rikl in the doubles although both appeared in the singles matches on Friday when they lost to Rafter and Philippoussis, respectively.
The two sides will play two reverse dead singles rubbers on Sunday.
Australia upset Davis Cup holders France, also on grass, in the previous round two months ago in Sydney.
